speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you are experiencing episodes of dizziness and vertigo; to help determine the cause, how long do these episodes typically last, and do you experience any hearing loss or ringing in your ears?

speaker: Patient
text: 70-year-old woman. The patient presents with sudden episodes of dizziness that are position dependent. She describes experiencing a false sensation of motion and occasional spinning, indicative of vertigo. She denies any recent illnesses, injuries, or significant changes in health status, apart from age-related hearing loss (presbycusis).

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information; the fact that your dizziness is position-dependent is a key detail. Are these episodes triggered specifically when you roll over in bed, stand up quickly, or lean back? Additionally, do you experience any new hearing loss, tinnitus, or nausea during these spells?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Episodes of dizziness and spinning sensation. I also have Position dependent vertigo, No recent illness, No hearing loss besides presbycusis.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV). The clinical presentation of sudden, position-dependent vertigo in a 70-year-old patient is classic for this condition. No further tests or questions are required to confirm this diagnosis.
